mercēnārius, mercēnāriī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a hired worker, an employee

Anyone working for pay (mercēs); a woman is mercēnāria (Traupman 309). Also written mercēnnārius (de Vaan 376: mercēn(n)ārius). Cicero counts wage-labour among the meaner livelihoods (Off. 1.150), so the word can sound low; for an office worker see minister.

Other words

  • minister, ministrī m. — an assistant; an employee

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Levi–Bini p. 33 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically a servant or attendant (Lewis & Short); Levi and Bini give it for an employee, with the periphrasis quī operam mercēde dat, one who works for pay.

Examples

  • Est autem īnfima condiciō et fortūna servōrum, quibus nōn male praecipiunt quī ita jubent ūtī, ut mercēnnāriīs, operam exigendam, jūsta praebenda.

    The lowest condition and lot is that of slaves, and those who tell us to treat them like hired workers give good advice: demand the work, give them what is fair.Cic. Off. 1.41

See also workman, job, manager.
